$comment: One note per engine behaviour, keyed by ref to the id in packages/engine's registry. The rules panel shows the engine's own id, label and cite; this file adds the sentence a player reads. scripts/labels-check.test.ts fails when a behaviour has no note or a note has no behaviour.
title: Rules panel notes
label: invention

records.text: One six-sided die. The book has no other.
Two dice read as a two-digit address, first die tens, second die ones: the Technique, Ritual and word tables.
Two dice summed, with both faces kept so a doubles result can be shown and a save replayed.
SKILL is 1d6+6, ENDURANCE 2d6+12, LUCK 1d6+6.
The rolled values are kept as the Master's initial values beside the current ones; later rules refer back to them.
One d6 for social status, and the gold that comes with it.
Common clothing, one weapon, and a Health Elixir or a Market item under 20 GP.
The free-text starting weapon counts as a weapon for any armed Proficiency.
records.says: a weapon, even if not listed in the weapon table
records.silent: which weapons count for which style
records.reversed: armed Proficiencies would add nothing until a Market weapon is bought

records.text: A Martial Art is chosen, or rolled on the banded d6 x d6 table of eighteen.
The points to spend on Proficiencies equal the rolled SKILL, before any Training is deducted from it.
No Proficiency may exceed 4 at creation.
Proficiency points may be left unspent, and a Proficiency may be left at zero.
records.says: spend as many points as your SKILL value
records.silent: whether every point must be spent
records.reversed: creation would flag every sheet with points left over

records.text: Each Training point bought at creation permanently lowers SKILL by one.
Each Training point gives four Resource points; a Technique or Ritual costs its printed value in them.
Training is carried as a Proficiency with a value, usable in checks.
Overspending a pool raises a flag with the numbers; the engine never refuses a creation.
The author's eight sheets load exactly as printed, flags and all; nothing is corrected.
2d6 against SKILL plus one relevant Proficiency; equal or under passes.
2d6 against LUCK; equal or under passes.
Every LUCK check costs one LUCK, pass or fail.
Two sixes fail a check whatever the threshold. Sealed in spec.md; reopening it is a re-seed.
Whether an action is a SKILL check or a LUCK check is the player's call; the engine offers both and picks neither.
Each side's Attack Strength is 2d6 plus SKILL plus one relevant Proficiency.
Exactly one Proficiency enters a roll, never two.
Training's value adds to checks made to perform or resist Techniques, not to Attack Strength.
records.says: use Training skill as one of your Martial Proficiency
records.reversed: every trained Master would roll higher in every round

records.text: Where a stat block lists two Proficiencies, the engine adds the higher unless the narrative or a Special result names the other.
records.silent: which of two, for a foe carrying both
records.reversed: every two-Proficiency foe would hit for less

records.text: When the opponent's total is higher, the Master loses the difference from ENDURANCE.
When the Master's total is higher, choose one: strike for the difference, use a Technique, change or recover a weapon, or create an Opening.
In combat a Technique is available only as the winner's option in a round; outside combat, at any time.
records.says: use one of the Techniques you know
records.silent: whether a Technique may be used when behind

records.text: A Technique used in combat needs no roll and costs its value in ENDURANCE.
Creating an Opening does no damage; it makes a Final Blow possible.
A fight ends when a Final Blow lands, either side's ENDURANCE reaches zero, or an Unexpected Event occurs.
After an Opening, roll 2d6; doubles land the blow, six chances in thirty-six.
A double six lands a doubles roll; the fumble rule is for checks only. Sealed in spec.md.
A landed Final Blow may become a new Technique: roll against LUCK, then give it a value of 1-4 and a description.
The Final Blow's LUCK roll costs one LUCK on a failure only; a success costs nothing.
records.silent: whether the ordinary LUCK-check decrement also applies
records.reversed: every kept Technique would cost a point of LUCK

records.text: A Praying Mantis Master's landed Final Blow kills; the doubles roll itself is unchanged.
records.silent: whether the style changes the roll or only the outcome
records.reversed: the Mantis would land blows more often instead of harder

records.text: The Final Blow table gives three words for inspiration; composing the name is the player's.
Equal Attack Strengths are an Unexpected Event.
After an Unexpected Event you are no longer in the combat phase; the 2d6 table is rolled only if the narrative leaves the event unclear.
Nine of the eleven rows state no mechanical effect; the engine carries a minimum reading for each and labels it so.
records.says: the row's text, and nothing else, for rows 2-5 and 9-12
records.silent: what an injury, a lost weapon or a divine intervention does to the numbers
records.reversed: those rows would be narration with no effect on the sheet

records.text: Row 7's 1-4 Minions are read off a d6: 1-2 one, 3 two, 4 three, 5-6 four.
records.silent: how to roll 1-4 in a d6-only game

records.text: The two Enemy-retreat rows roll Morale on a d6: 1-3 it flees, 4-5 a cautious retreat, 6 it rallies with 1d6 more. Ours, sealed in spec.md.
Against several opponents the Master's SKILL is reduced by their number.
An opponent's ATTACK is how many of its kind may attack at once.
ATTACK counts opponents a creature can wound at once and does nothing against a lone Master. Sealed in spec.md.
The one stat block printed with a blank ATTACK is read as 1.
In multiple combat the Master rolls once a round and that roll is compared against each attacker's own roll.
records.says: reduce your SKILL by the number of opponents
records.reversed: one roll per opponent, and a very different fight

records.text: An area Technique deals the same damage to each opponent it reaches, not a share of it.
How many opponents an area Technique reaches is read from its printed text: two, or all around.
records.says: Butterfly Palms, Light Body, Exploding Qi, Double Strike
records.reversed: every area Technique would reach the same count

records.text: Fleeing without a stratagem costs a last blow of 2 ENDURANCE.
Each escape that costs damage scores one Dishonor Point.
A stratagem is any escape Technique or a player-declared one the Oracle approves; the last blow is damage, so a bare escape always scores Dishonor.
records.says: a Technique or some other stratagem
records.silent: what counts, and whether the last blow is damage
records.reversed: a bare escape would cost ENDURANCE but no Dishonor

records.text: SKILL recovers one point from a regeneration Technique and fully after a night's rest.
ENDURANCE recovers four from a healing Technique, a meal or an Elixir, and fully after a week's rest.
LUCK recovers one point from a Spirituality check at a Temple, with incense.
The book gives LUCK no full restore, so the engine invents none.
A night's rest heals 4 ENDURANCE. Ours, sealed in spec.md.
At an adventure's end, four scores of 1-3 are summed and Dishonor subtracted: that is the XP.
What an advance costs depends on the Master's SKILL band.
The band is read from current SKILL at the moment of spending.
records.says: the worked example uses the current value
records.reversed: a Master whose SKILL fell would pay a different price

records.text: SKILL and LUCK cannot exceed 12.
After creation a Proficiency may rise past 4.
Unspent XP waits for the next advancement.
The four scores are the player's own; the engine flags an odd total and refuses nothing.
A defeated opponent's treasure is 1d6 on the band its ENDURANCE falls in.
The treasure roll is always offered after a victory and may be declined.
records.says: if you believe that your defeated opponents may be in possession of something
records.reversed: the app would have to guess when a foe carries anything

records.text: A spirit or ghost is immune to ordinary blows; a Technique, Ritual or exceptional weapon is needed.
An opponent's Martial Arts (n) gives every Proficiency n points; its Techniques add their value with no ENDURANCE cost.
The Oracle's Special enemy attack uses one of the opponent's listed Proficiencies this round.
An Oracle Ambush is one unopposed opening round for the opponent.
records.says: Ambush and Attack as two outcomes
records.reversed: Ambush and Attack would play identically

records.text: The book throws dice on a sheet of paper; the app places each point from dice so a saved region lands the same way twice.
records.says: roll a handful of d6 on a sheet of paper; mark where the dice land
records.silent: how an app without paper does that
records.reversed: a region could not be replayed from its record

records.text: Each point's Location is the face its die shows, read on the Region table.
Points are linked to their nearest neighbours. Ours.
Where nearest-neighbour links leave islands, the closest pair across the gap is joined so the region can be walked. Ours; joined links are marked.
A link's miles are the sum of the two dice that measured it; the book calls the scale arbitrary. Ours.
The same 2d6 reads the route type on the book's table: nothing, mule track, trail, beaten path, paved road.
Where a point sits on the screen means nothing; the diagram says it is not to scale. Ours.
